transcript_full: Welcome to Doha. The first thing that I do after the match is debrief with my [music] with my team. Obviously, hug my family members if they're present to to watch me play. [music] I'll do my rehab, I'll do stretch, I'll do some active recovery, and uh I'll do my ice bath, I'll do some manual work with my physiotherapist, and of course, get a good nutrition and hydration in, and just uh you know, go on with my day. One habit that kept me through my highs and lows is a good walk in the nature. Touching the ground with my bare feet is something that is so simple, [music] but so yet so effective. And uh just being outdoors, to be honest, whatever the weather is, uh cuz, you know, [music] we're constantly with screens and indoor. So, you know, particularly when I'm not feeling really myself, you know, mentally, physically, emotionally, I just like to go out, bike ride, or jog, or just walk in the nature and let the nature do its job. Obviously, trying to get some sleep if it's a long flight. Enjoying my entertainment. Reading a good book never disappoints. [music] And uh I also like I like to write. You know, for a lot of people, including myself, flying [music] and being in the plane up in the air just awakens the creative side of you. I've been traveling for, well, 30 years, and >> [music] >> quite intense traveling for tennis. It's quite essential for me as a professional athletes to frequently stretching and hydrating myself, and you know, keeping up with with my body's needs. You just have to accept it. Intensity of the jet lag depends on how you take care of [music] yourself. Obviously, that determines of how jet lag you are. So, I try to obviously set my time zone for where I'm headed and just really having the right mindset about it and getting adapted and adjusted to the environment where when you arrive. It's okay to think that it's relaxing because it is, particularly if you're sitting in a comfortable seat. But, at the same time, you know, if we if we feel too comfortable, then we forget about some of the other things that are essential for the long flights, particularly which is movement and hydration. Even when I think I'm hydrated, I will hydrate even more cuz I think that when you're hydrated well, then everything else is set in motion physiologically. But, it also sets your clock, I think your circadian rhythm better, so your sleep-wake [music] cycle. And then taking a little walk in the aisle, it still does does its wonders. Hydration is essential for our survival. I mean, we have to hydrate ourselves in order to [music] to live. Drinking plain water is always great. It's always very good. On the flights, often times [music] because of the cabin pressure and lack of oxygen, people feel more dehydrated. So, it's more important than anywhere else to hydrate on the plane. And [music] that's where hydration formula and electrolytes come into into equation. That's why I created Sila because hydration is such a crucial element [music] and Sila hydration formula provides you with all the essential ingredients for your everyday life. >> [music] >> Wellness is a lifestyle. It's also mindset, I think. taking care of yourself, of your body. It's a balance between your mind, body, and soul. >> [music] >> It's quite relative for all of us, you know, leading different lifestyles. I think there are some basic needs and things that that we all need to respect [music] in order to live the healthiest lives possible, which is hydration, nutrition, sleep, managing all of that, and taking care of yourself will definitely give you a springboard for a healthier and happier life. Sila by Novak, available on board Qatar Airways.

title: This Chef Is Bringing Hong Kong's Flavours to the Skies
transcript_excerpt: It's braised for many hours and it falls apart very easily.…
transcript_full: Why food?  I love watching people enjoy the food and share their time with each other.  Food is the ultimate universal language.  Hi, I'm Vicky Lau, chef of Tay Tining Room in Hong Kong.  So we're here today in collaboration with Qatar Airways to create an insight dining experience.  We've created a first in business class menu with different courses,  a bit of highlight of East and West, the kind of dishes that we make in Hong Kong.  So first we have a chicken roulade, and it's made from local yellow chicken,  which is one of our favorite chicken in Hong Kong.  Roll into a roulade and then dip into a sauce marinated and then steamed together.  This little dish has a lot of different kinds of flavor in the sauce as well as the umami of the chicken  and a surf cold along with some cucumber and mushroom.  We use very fresh ingredient.  We love fresh ingredients in Hong Kong and I think this is a very innovative dish  that is representative of Hong Kong gastron.  The second dish is a beef cheek that's been braised in a grape juice as well as many different spices  and dried fruits.  It's braised for many hours and it falls apart very easily.  It's soft together with some rice and it's very comforting and flavorful.  So the third dish at dessert, which is featuring one of my two favorite fruits,  which is the mango and passion fruit, goes together perfectly in a very smooth moose into a cake  and a bit of a sponge at the bottom, crispy to the top, just melts in your mouth and it's flavorful.  So the fourth dish is a chicken and abalone rice.  It's a very comforting dish with chicken and abalone being the feature of a lot of umami  and just warm rice mixed together.  It's what someone would like to eat at home.  Creating a dish for insight is a bit challenging because you have to create many different things,  different flavors within one tray and we have to think about the technique, how it's being reheated,  still showing the flavors and different freshness of the ingredient.  The thing that excites me the most about Hong Kong dining scene is the diversity.  You can find all kinds of Chinese food and as well as many different cultures.  So in Hong Kong we like to mix the best together.  I hope that they would get a glimpse of Hong Kong gastronomy, a bit of east and west,  a little journey into Hong Kong and experience all the different kinds of ingredients that we have here.

title: How do you move Beluga Whales across a continent?

transcript_full: [music] >> Have you ever wondered how an animal from the ocean can board a plane? >> Transporting beluga whales is really complicated. Here we're dealing with really big animals and a lot of water, cold water temperatures. >> Cranes and stretchers and trucks and planes, [music] every little detail has been planned out. >> For these beluga whales, this is no ordinary flight. Their future in Canada had become uncertain. And an international rescue effort was formed to move them safely toward new homes in the United States. With Qatar Airways Cargo, a journey that would usually happen through water is about to unfold through the sky. Yes, whales on a plane. It sounds unbelievable, but that's exactly what's about to happen. >> I am one of a group of veterinarians who specialize in the care of marine mammals, [music] who have learned about their medical history, will be taking care of them throughout the transport and after they arrive to their new home. Everyone from the Marineland staff who've been taking care of them for [music] years to all of the people at the easy institutions around the world just want what's best for them. >> [music] >> Here we'll be carefully loading them into specialized animal transport [music] containers that are built specifically for beluga whales. They'll Those will be positioned on trucks. Those trucks will then be attended [music] by veterinarians and animal care specialists while we transport them [music] very carefully to the airport where they'll be gently loaded onto an aircraft and flown directly [music] to their new destination. So that might look like having extra trucks that are just following along in case there's a mechanical difficulty. >> [music] [music] >> Transporting any animal is a huge responsibility. [music] Transporting something to this scale, of this importance, and with [music] the the responsibilities involved, it's really hard to put into words what this project means. >> For these whales, while their physical location may be changing [music] from Canada to the United States, dedication and care for them does not stop. And we are so excited to welcome [music] them to Shedd and continue to care for them throughout their life. >> [music] >> So, we've been thinking about all the different ways that we're going to prep [music] them physically, socially, mentally. We want them to transport safely, and we want to watch them integrate [music] into their new pods and be belugas. >> [applause] >> It's impossible to know everything, especially in a timely rescue [music] like this. title: Festive Flight and Christmas Layover in Vienna as Emirates Cabin Crew
transcript_excerpt: Hi, I'm Ariana and I'm Emirates cabin crew. It's the most wonderful time of the year and I'm getting…
transcript_full: Hi, I'm Ariana and I'm Emirates cabin crew. It's the most wonderful time of the year and I'm getting  ready for a 24 hour layover in Vienna. Come along and see what my festive flight looks like.  The Christmas season looks a little bit different in Dubai so I'm always excited to see  European destination on my roster in December. We arrive at the aircraft and begin our pre-boarding  jet. And how cool is this? The entire month of December we have mood lighting and some Christmas  classics playing to really make the cabin a little bit more festive. Customers start boarding  and the festivities begin. One of my favourite parts about flying around Christmas time is getting  a little bit dressed up and putting together surprises for our customers. We take our role very  seriously. We serve up some delicious hot chocolate with gingerbread and to capture the Christmas  magic we snap some polaroids for our customers to keep. After finally landing in Vienna I'm wasting  no time. First things first I check into the hotel and change into some warm clothes.  Now I'm ready to soak up the Christmas vibes for myself. Vienna is home to some of the oldest  and most iconic Christmas markets in the world. The most famous of them all is located here  in Rathouse Blast. The market is full of traditional stores that are perfect for window shopping  and foodies come with an empty stomach. No matter if you're into sweet or savory there's  something yummy for everyone. I grab myself a hot chocolate and take a wander through the rest  of the market. Check out all of these beautiful festivities like installations. After strolling past  every stall and eating way too much it's time to head back to the hotel and that's a wrap on my 24  hours in Vienna. A short but very sweet trip that definitely delivered festive. Thanks for joining me,  Merry Christmas!

title: Emirates A380 business class flight review ✨ #emirates #businessclass
transcript_excerpt: We got some slippers and an eye mask and also we had some headphones and so much leg room.…

captions.text: We got some slippers and an eye mask and also we had some headphones and so much leg room.

transcript_full: Flying on Emma at Z380 was high on my bucket list and we finally got to do this on our flight back from  Koala Lumpur on the second leg from Debye to London Heathrow in business class.  It was a 1-2-1 configuration and we got the two seats that were closest together.  We got some slippers and an eye mask and also we had some headphones and so much leg room.  There were some water and snacks at the seat and we got a blanket and fluffy pillow and also a  Bulgarian menatee kit and I was so happy because I've seen so many videos of people in opening these  so I just couldn't believe I finally got my own.  Crew brought around the Y menu and food menu and then shortly made the seat into a bed and by  this point I was really flagging from the flight before so I was appreciative.  I then got settled and had a Kerai Allen some warm notes and then I got the Arabic menatee to start  with a glass of red and Anthony had the prawn starter. We then both had the steak which was really  nice but the thing I was most looking forward to about flying the A380 was the onboard bar.  Someone that other than this trip was only ever flown economy I was over the moon because where else  can you drink cocktails in the sky. We was traveling for about 14 hours by this point so I was  flagging but it was absolutely nowhere I was missing out on this experience.  Emirates include a show for service so when we landed at Heathrow we followed the signs and  I just felt so bougie to be able to do this. They then take you to this little lounge where you can  get drinks and snacks and best believe this was the end of our trip so I did take some for the  journey. The we then had the loveliest man pickers up. This was an absolute 10-10 experience and I  need to find a way to do it again.

transcript_excerpt: I boarded, found my seat 5K, a rear facing seat by the way so that's a first for me.…
transcript_full: This is the business class that I've been stalking online for years and I finally got to fly it.  Qatar Airways Q-Suite.  Possibly the best in the sky and I flown a few.  I boarded, found my seat 5K, a rear facing seat by the way so that's a first for me.  And immediately got comfortable in my seat.  Shortly after, welcome drink in my hand.  And we hadn't even taken off yet.  Just how I like it.  Now the menu.  Plenty of choices.  And the best part, dine on demand.  Order what you want, when you want it.  Getting hungry at 3 a.m. they got you.  But it was a midnight flight so my first move was to get some sleep.  I checked out the pajamas that they handed me and I quickly got to changing and I mean super quick.  I liked them so much that I actually kept them.  No regrets.  Shortly after, I tucked myself in, closed my door and I was out like a light.  Walk up and had my first meal.  Korean chicken and fried rice.  10 out of 10, possibly the best choice in my opinion.  And right after, I did a little skin care because self care doesn't stop at cruising  altitude.  Then, I knocked out again.  Walk up shortly and I ordered myself a cream cheese omelette with karak on the side.  Somehow also incredible.  And right before landing, one more karak.  Because you cannot.  And I repeat, you cannot have too much karak.  Secondly, one of the best experiences I've had in the sky.  So glad that I finally have the chance to check it out.

title: Why Qatar Airways Flies Empty Boeing 777s in Australia #facts #history
transcript_excerpt: It turns around, flies back empty, and picks up a whole new crowd of international travelers in Melbourne.…

captions.text: It turns around, flies back empty, and picks up a whole new crowd of international travelers in Melbourne.

transcript_full: Have you ever wondered why a massive 354-seat Boeing 777 flies almost completely empty across Australia every single morning?  At 5.35 a.m. daily, Qatar Airways Flight QR-988 takes off from Melbourne to Adelaide, carrying virtually zero passengers.  This isn't an accident, but rather a brilliant loophole designed to trick Australian aviation law.  To protect local carrier Qantas, Australia caps Qatar Airways to just 28 weekly flights into major hubs like Melbourne.  However, flights to smaller, regional cities like Adelaide remain completely uncapped.  So, in November 2022, Qatar registered a daily flight from Doha to Adelaide, but rooted it with a layover in Melbourne.  Here's the catch. Australian law strictly forbids foreign airlines from selling tickets for purely domestic routes.  When the giant jet lands in Melbourne, almost every international passenger disembarks.  Because no local passengers can board, the 354-seat Boeing 777 must fly 400 miles to Adelaide nearly empty.  It turns around, flies back empty, and picks up a whole new crowd of international travelers in Melbourne.  Qatar's successfully unlocked an extra high-value flight slot in Melbourne,  but leaves a daily trail of massive carbon waste.

title: How profitable is an Etihad 787 flight? #etihad #aviation #business

transcript_full: If you take an Etihad Boeing 787 from Abu Dhabi to London, you might wonder how much money the  airline actually makes from one flight. This route takes around 7 hours and 40 minutes, covering roughly  5,500 kilometres. This aircraft has 32 business class seats and 271 economy seats. Let's assume  the aircraft is 90% full. Business class could bring in around $41,000, while economy could bring in  roughly $126,000, giving the flight around $167,000 from passengers. The aircraft can also  carry cargo in its belly, so $15,000 from cargo. That brings the total estimated revenue to around  $182,000. Then we have fuel, crew, airport fees, catering, maintenance and other operating costs,  which could cost roughly $140,000. So, after all those expenses, Etihad can make around $42,000  in estimated profit from a single flight.

title: Why the doors wouldn't open on Saudia Flight 163 #aviation #history #scary
transcript_excerpt: The first door on this plane was open 26 minutes after it stopped from outside.…
transcript_full: The first door on this plane was open 26 minutes after it stopped from outside.  With the power off, every door opened from outside with one handle.  Saudi a flight 163 landed at Riyadh with a fire on board.  No door was open from inside and none of the three of one on board survived.  The fireman, the report says, did as well as they were able to,  but lacked the training and equipment.  At the front left door, a man on a truck ladder pulled the handle.  He couldn't be sure the door moved.  At the front right door, the handle couldn't be found under the foam.  Then a fireman opened the second door on the right.  Its inside emergency handle had never been used.

chapters.title: オープニング：ANAマイルプレゼントキャンペーンの概要
前置き：今月のその他キャンペーン（減額マイル・タイムセール等）の省略について
本題：「乗るたび、次の旅へ ANA国内線特典航空券マイルプレゼントキャンペーン」の紹介
注意点①：登録期間（5/25〜7/17）と予約・発券期間（5/26以降）のズレ
注意点②：乗り継ぎ区間のカウント方法（出発地から最終目的地までを1区間として算出）
注意点③：ANA国際線特典・提携会社特典の国内線区間、トクたびマイル、減額マイルは対象外
キャンペーンがお得ではない最大の理由：ANAマイル（レギュラー8,500）とユナイテッド航空（UA）マイル（7,000）の必要マイル数比較

UAマイル発券における重大な変更点：AIRDO、スターフライヤー、ソラシドエア等の提携航空会社便が予約不可になった事実
提携便のみ就航の地方空港（旭川、帯広、北九州等）への影響とUAサイトでの検索エラー検証
ANA国際線特典航空券と提携航空会社特典航空券における提携便（AIRDO等）の利用可否ルールの検証
キャンペーン条件のおさらいと、マイル（ANA、UA、マリオット等）を分散保有するメリット
発券マイル種別や普通運賃による機内サービス・扱いの差は一切ないことの解説
今回のキャンペーンを活用すべき具体的なケース（AIRDO指定や地方空港利用時など）と総括
エンディング：チャンネル登録と高評価の案内

title: Strangest business seat (Philippine Airlines)🫣🇵🇭
transcript_excerpt: First off, there's no inflight entertainment as you can see.…
transcript_full: Here are some of the crazy things about what I consider to be the most unique business  cost seat in the world, and let's just say flying it is an experience.  But wait to see how much I paid because I might actually still be worth it.  I got to enjoy this wild Philippine Airlines seat on an almost 10 hour flight from Manila  to the Middle East.  Meaning I had plenty of time to realize just how strange this is.  First off, there's no inflight entertainment as you can see.  Yeah, there are no screens, but they also don't even hand out tablets on a 10 hour flight.  What does this enable the airline to do?  They let them push the seats even closer together since essentially the seats are stacked.  Once the reclives into a bed very low to the ground and the other seat half way to the ceiling.  Basically you're sleeping with your legs above the other person.  You also don't really have any storage on the side since they're climbing six seats  in per row when economy normally has eight seats per row on this same aircraft type.  Would you try this seat?  How about if you only had to pay $750 for this 10 hour flight?  It's currently bookable for that, so if your answer was yes, you might want to check  that deal out.

title: How the showers work in Emirates A380 First Class
transcript_excerpt: Here's how the MRTA3D first-class shower experience works. There are 14 first-class seats on their A3D and two showers,…
transcript_full: Here's how the MRTA3D first-class shower experience works. There are 14 first-class seats on their A3D and two showers,  so it's usually not a problem for everyone to get to use it. As it started the flight, the crew will ask what time you want to shower,  and you can pretty much request any time during the flight. Once it's your turn, the shower will be prepared for you,  meaning the floors have been heated, thousand toiletries have been laid out, and you've received your shower bag with  slippers, pajamas, and your Bulgari amenity kit. The shower feels surprisingly spacious, and even has a small seat  inside, so theoretically you can spend as long as you want in here, but obviously you shouldn't, and you're  limited to 5 minutes of running water. Luckily, this dial makes it easy to track how much of your water you've used,  and if you turn the water off, the timer stops as well. After your shower, there's even a hair dryer in here.  Flying doesn't get better than this.

Yeah, there are no screens, but they also don't even hand out tablets on a 10 hour flight.  What does this enable the airline to do?  They let them push the seats even closer together since essentially the seats are stacked.  Once the reclives into a bed very low to the ground and the other seat half way to the ceiling.  Basically you're sleeping with your legs above the other person.  You also don't really have any storage on the side since they're climbing six seats  in per row when economy normally has eight seats per row on this same aircraft type.  Would you try this seat?  How about if you only had to pay $750 for this 10 hour flight?  It's currently bookable for that, so if your answer was yes, you might want to check  that deal out.

title: How the showers work in Emirates A380 First Class
transcript_excerpt: Here's how the MRTA3D first-class shower experience works. There are 14 first-class seats on their A3D and two showers,…
transcript_full: Here's how the MRTA3D first-class shower experience works. There are 14 first-class seats on their A3D and two showers,  so it's usually not a problem for everyone to get to use it. As it started the flight, the crew will ask what time you want to shower,  and you can pretty much request any time during the flight. Once it's your turn, the shower will be prepared for you,  meaning the floors have been heated, thousand toiletries have been laid out, and you've received your shower bag with  slippers, pajamas, and your Bulgari amenity kit. The shower feels surprisingly spacious, and even has a small seat  inside, so theoretically you can spend as long as you want in here, but obviously you shouldn't, and you're  limited to 5 minutes of running water. Luckily, this dial makes it easy to track how much of your water you've used,  and if you turn the water off, the timer stops as well. After your shower, there's even a hair dryer in here.  Flying doesn't get better than this.

title: The little known Tijuana border crossing trick | 1-Minute Flight Review–Volaris Economy
transcript_excerpt: During the two times I've traveled through a Mexican airport, passenger boarding has been…
transcript_full: Good day, welcome back to the Flying Dr Channel.  On today's one minute flight review, I'll take you on board Valeris headed to Tijuana  from Mazitlan.  Once airside a single departure lounge splits off into two wings of gates.  There's not much on either wing of the airport, so get your snacks and food prior to heading  to the gate.  Once at the gate, you'll likely find a zoo of humans waiting to board.  During the two times I've traveled through a Mexican airport, passenger boarding has been  worse than it is in the states.  We were lucky enough to board from the ramp which made up for the slight departure  delay.  Once on board I found myself squished in a window seat with little room.  Before we push back, a quick shadow boxing match appeared out my window.  The wind direction and single runway Mazitlan uses means we are back-taxing today before  departing to the west.  As we tracked north along the eastern Gulf of California coast, I wondered if any service  would be offered.  As an ultra-low-cost carrier, everything is for purchase.  Water, however, is available for free.  The whole purpose of this flight was to test out the CBX or Cross-Border Express, a unique  land bridge that connects to the California of the airport.  As we made our descent, I began to think about how I would explain to the customs agent  why I decided to fly from Washington, D.C. to Minneapolis, Mexico City, Mazitlan, and  finally to Yohana when my final destination was San Diego.  After following all of the signs, I made it to the gate, crossed the bridge, met with  customs, and was granted reentry into the country.  A painless process for anyone living around San Diego looking to fly in or out of Tijuana.  As always, thanks for watching.  See ya!

title: 10 Secret Hacks for a FLIGHT UPGRADE
transcript_excerpt: Solo travelers are much easier to upgrade than couples or families.…

captions.text: Solo travelers are much easier to upgrade than couples or families.

transcript_full: Here's a list of ten secret hacks that can boost your chances of getting a flight upgrade,  whether to business or even first class.  These aren't guaranteed, but they definitely increase your odds.  One, join the Airlines Loyalty Program.  Even if you don't fly often, sign up for the Airlines Frequent Flyer Program.  Those upgrades go to anyone in the loyalty system, not just elites.  Two, dress the part.  Airlines are more likely to upgrade passengers who look the part.  Think clean, business casual attire.  No flip flops or sweats if you're angling for business class.  Three, check in, late, strategically.  If the flight is overbooked in economy, checking in closer to departure might help.  Those may upgrade the last passengers to balance the cabin, especially if you're solo.  Four, ask nicely, just say, hi, I was wondering if there are any complimentary upgrades available  today.  Do this politely and privately at check-in or the gate.  Kindness can work wonders.  Five, travel solo.  Solo travelers are much easier to upgrade than couples or families.  If you're alone, you're a great fit for a single empty seat in business class.  Six, pick flights with lower premium cabin load, use tools like expert flyer, seat guru,  or Google flights to check seat maps.  Flights with empty business slash first seats are your best bet.  Seven, use credit card perks premium travel cards like Amix Platinum, Chase Sapphire Reserve,  or airline co-branded cards often come with upgrade eligibility or priority boarding,  a big plus.  Eight, don't sit near babies.  If possible, some agents use this to determine potential upgrades, moving passengers away  from crying infants to improve comfort in higher cabins.  Nine, mention special occasions, subtly, a honeymoon, anniversary, or milestone birthday  might tip the scales.  Mention it in a casual, genuine way, not with entitlement.  Ten, book direct with the airline booking directly, instead of through OTAs, gives airline  staff more flexibility to modify your reservation, including upgrades.

title: How to Book Cheapest Flight Tickets
transcript_excerpt: Prices can drop significantly during off-peak travel times, so research the best times…
transcript_full: Booking the cheapest flight tickets can be a bit of a science, but here are some effective  strategies to help you save.  1.  Use flight comparison websites.  Start with sites like Google Flites, Skyscanner or Kayak to compare prices across multiple  airlines.  2.  Be flexible with dates.  If possible, search for flights on different dates.  Midweek flights, Tuesday or Wednesday are often cheaper than weekend departures.  3.  Set fare alerts.  Use tools that notify you when prices drop for your desired route.  Book in advance.  Generally, booking one to three months in advance can yield better prices, though it can vary  based on the destination and season.  5.  Consider nearby airports.  Check flights to and from nearby airports.  You might find a better deal that way.  6.  Using Cognito Mode.  When searching for flights, use your browsers in Cognito Mode to prevent price increases  based on your search history.  7.  Look for budget airlines.  Don't overlook budget carriers.  Just be aware of additional fees for baggage and seat selection.  8.  Check for promotions.  Follow airlines on social media and subscribe to their newsletters for exclusive deals and  flash sales.  9.  Be open to layovers.  Direct flights are convenient, but flights with layovers can often be cheaper.  10.  Travel during off-peak seasons.  Prices can drop significantly during off-peak travel times, so research the best times  to visit your destination.  11.  Use points or miles.  If you have frequent flyer miles or credit card points, redeeming them can greatly reduce  costs.  12.  Consider package deals.  Sometimes booking flights with hotels or car rentals can offer discounts.  By combining these strategies, you can maximize your chances of finding the cheapest flights.  Happy Travels!

title: HONEST Review of Qantas A380 First Class from LA to Sydney #shorts  #firstclass #airline
transcript_excerpt: Even the most comfortable way to fly nonstop from the US to Australia has its issues.…
transcript_full: Even the most comfortable way to fly nonstop from the US to Australia has its issues.  Come with me as I fly home to Sydney for the holidays in Qantas A380 First Class.  After connecting through LAX, I headed straight to the Qantas International First Lounge.  While I enjoyed Neil Perry's famous salt and pepper squid, the lounge experience was  disappointing thanks to lackluster food, woeful water pressure in the showers and no standout  first class perks. But it was still a thrill to board this superjumbo. The first class  cabin is expansive with 14 open suites in a spacious 111 configuration. Even though this  product underwent a refresh during the pandemic, these seats still lag behind its competitors,  particularly without the all-important sliding door. But the seat is wide and the suite has a ton of  space so you won't feel cramped at all. After takeoff, I dived into a multicost dinner featuring  crab soup and a Middle Eastern style couscous main, followed by a rhubarb dessert, truffles,  and ginger tea. But just like in the lounge, the food wasn't anything exciting. What did shine?  Was the bed. The plush mattress top up, breathable, cozy bedding, and built-in annozzles make  this bed a standout, even amongst the likes of Emirates, ANA and Singapore. I woke up to breakfast  as we prepared for our landing. This ticket was booked for 135,000 katha pacific Asia miles,  and just under $200 in taxes. If you're headed down under, business class is more than enough for  most passengers. But if you can snag rare a water availability and have the points,  once as first is worth it.
